newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

CANADA, Dec 9 - Vancouver, BC - GRAIN - 5 Vessels loading, 8 waiting, 7-14 days delay depending on grade to be loaded. 16 Vessels due by end-December. Roberts Bank - COAL - 2 Vessels loading, 18 due to load by end-December, 13 scheduled for January loading. Prince Rupert - GRAIN - 3 Vessels awaiting cargo, delays of approx. 7-14 days depending on grade to be loaded. Halifax, NS - No congestion or delays. The shipyards and Dartmouth are available for ship repairs.

HONDURAS, Dec 10 - Puerto Cortes - Two vessels berthed of which 1 each discharging fertiliser, soya. 15 Vessels due of which 10 to discharge/load containers, 5 to load bananas, no berthing delays expected. Vessels berthed, 3 Discharging/loading containers, 1 discharging general cargo, 1 discharging sorghum/corn, 1 discharging fuel. Vessels awaiting berth, 2 to discharge/load containers, 1 to discharge generals, 1 to discharge containers/load bananas. Vessels due, 6 to discharge/load containers, 5 to discharge/load generals, 4 to load bananas.

MEXICO, Dec 10 - Tampico - Vessels in port, 1 coke, 1 iron, 1 steel coils, 2 gasoline, 1 lpg gas. 3 Vessels anchored of which 2 corn, 1 gasoline, working normally. Altamira - Vessels in port, 1 chemical, working normally. Veracruz - Vessels in port, 1 steel coils, 2 sugar, 3 pipes, 4 grain, 1 repair, 2 general cargo, working normally. Manzanlo - Vessels in port, 3 general cargo, 2 cars, 2 containers, 2 grain, working normally. Coatzacoalcos - Vessels in port, 9 chemicals, 6 oil tankers, working normally.

PANAMA, Dec 10 - Balboa - Vessels operating, 1 bulker, 1 fishing vessel, 1 tanker. Cristobal - Vessels operating, 2 containers, 1 general, 1 tanker. Panama Canal - The Panama Canal commission has announced simultaneous locks lane outages from 15/12 to 19/12 and are projecting 28-30 daily transits. During this period, delays of about 3 days could be encountered depending on the amount of vessels arriving for transit. Waterway at full capacity and transit booking system allocation normal until 15/12 to 19/12 at Gatun locks, and 16/12 to 19/12 at Pedro Miguel and Miraflores. Relay lockages and crew augmentation will be provided to minimise delays and the booking provisions will be reviewed as necessary. The backlog queue is high 10/12 due to the level of arrivals recently and the outages at Miraflores and Pedro Miguel locks. 41 Vessels due, 47 in queue, 16 booked, 41 scheduled. Very heavy rain.

UNITED STATES, Dec 9 - Port Newark, NJ - One vessel in port. Port Elizabeth - Two vessels in port. Bayway, NJ - One vessel in port. Cartaret, NJ - Two vessels in port. Hampton Roads, VA - Seven general cargo/container vessels in pier working. 2 Vessels at pier loading coal, 1 anchored waiting to load, 1 at pier on layberth arrangement. 1 Vessel discharging salt at pier, 1 at pier loading grain. 1 Anchored waiting to load, 1 vessel at pier loading fertiliser, 1 anchored waiting to load. Baltimore, MD - Vessels operating in port, 7 bulkers, 2 container, 1 ro/ro, 2 auto, 2 tankers, 3 general cargo, 3 cable on standby. 3 Vessels in repair yard, 2 bulkers awaiting berth.

Dec 10 - Honolulu, HI - Harbour - 2 Container vessels alongside, 4 tugs and barges alongside, no vessels at anchorage. Barbers Point, HI - One coal vessel alongside, 2 barges alongside. Offport mooring - 1 Tanker discharger. SOUTH COAST - Baltimore, MD - No congestion expected at Dundalk terminal this week, no adverse conditions at Candd canal. Baltimore harbour - Low ceiling. Elevators and coal operations have no delays, average waiting time Consul coal 5 days. Liquid bulk facilities - Operating normally, no berthing congestion. Anchorage clear at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC - No vessels due at coal terminal or grain elevator. No delays expected at tanker terminals and other terminals. No navigation problems in the harbour. Dredging in the north Charleston terminal could cause some delays.

Jacksonville, FL - No heavy berth congestion or delays at the port or at Fernandina beach, FL. Miami, FL - No congestion at container berths, gantry berths or ro/ro berths. Passenger terminals in full operation. New York, NY - No congestion at anchorages, container, tanker or sugar terminals. Norfolk, VA - 16 Vessels due at Norfolk southern coal pier. 1 Vessel anchored waiting to load, 8 due at Dominion terminal. 3 Vessels due at Pier IX. Coal terminal - 1 Vessel due at Cargill. Container and general cargo terminals working normally, as well as oil and bulk terminals. All channels are opening with prevailing depths available. A new independent marine terminal has the ability to handle small container and breakbulk vessels. Philadelphia, PA - No congestion in the port nor at Camden, Wilmington. No activity as far as dredging, repairs or navigation problems.

Savannah, GA - The Georgia ports authority expects heavy congestion at Garden City terminals in early part of week. By mid-week most of the congestion should have eased. Moderate congestion forecast for Ocean terminals throughout the week. 1-2 days delay for bulk clay terminals. No congestion at liquid bulk facilities. Navigational conditions remain normal. Vessels may expected some delays due to fog. On 27/11 an 800 ft. container vessel departing Savannah en route to the Panama Canal collided with the Savannah light tower located about 9 miles off shore at the entrance to the Savannah river. The tower was destroyed and the vessel lost a container containing 55 gallon drums of paint. The container and all the wreckage from the tower were found and salvage operations have commenced. Mariners are advised to take extreme caution when transiting this area. The coast guard has established a 1,000 yard safety zone around the sunken tower. The wreck area is also marked by buoys.

GULF COAST - Houston - No congestion at city docks and Galveston grain elevators. Congestion in some oil/chemical terminals. Mobile, AL - No berth/terminal congestion expected at either private or state-owned facilities. Some slight delays can be expected in main channel for both in/out traffic due to weather. Maintenance dredging continues in main ship channel. New Orleans, LA - Rain causes delays for grain loading. River stage at 11.3 ft, expected to rise to 12-5 ft. by 15/12. Normal transit times can be expected. Present max. permissible draft at the SW Pass is 47 ft. fw. for vessels under 100,000 dwt. 46 Ft. fw. for vessels over 100,000 dwt. Some elevators are not working weekends due to slower than usual grain shipments.

WEST COAST - Columbia River - 19 Grain vessels in the Columbia River district of which 7 loading, 12 waiting with average waiting time of 3-5 days at most elevators. Coos Bay - One nickel discharging, 2 woodchip carriers loading for Japanese discharge. 1 Log vessel loading at Ocean terminals, 1 lumber vessel loading. Long Beach, CA - Metropolitan - Moderately busy for December. 2-3 Days delay expected at anchorage for vessels awaiting berth. Koch Carbon - 1 Vessel due. Kaiser - 2-3 Days delay expected for coal/petcoke. Moderately busy in Los Angeles/Long Beach for bulk cargoes. No work will be performed from 1500 hours 24/12 to 0700 hours 26/12. San Francisco - Weather in the Pacific is slowing down. Vessels arriving, some delays are expected. No significant delays at the grain elevators. Anchorages open, but busy.
